title: What followed
hook: The German Confederation created a new federal order; imperial places outlived the institution.
notes: GHDI German Federal Act (1815) for Frankfurt and the named free cities; Habsburger Congress of Vienna history for the new order; UNESCO Aachen and Regensburg for surviving heritage. Heritage locators are reviewed at cutoff, not a claim of current territorial sovereignty. Coordinates are approximate named-place locators, not imported surveyed points. Modern borders are hidden. Event cards contain claim-level citations. The later term Holy Roman Empire must not be projected unchanged onto Charlemagne’s Frankish realm.

scenes.title: A settlement in Vienna
scenes.text: In 1815 the Congress of Vienna created the German Confederation. It followed the dissolved empire but did not restore its imperial crown.

scenes.title: The assembly moves to Frankfurt
scenes.text: The 1815 Federal Act placed the confederal assembly at Frankfurt. Comparing Vienna with Frankfurt separates the diplomatic settlement from the new institution’s meeting place.

scenes.title: Free cities in the new order
scenes.text: The Federal Act lists Lübeck, Frankfurt, Bremen and Hamburg alongside member states. The northern city anchors show continuity of some urban political identities within a different federal arrangement.

scenes.title: Buildings after institutions
scenes.text: Aachen’s chapel and Regensburg’s old town preserve traces of earlier imperial life. These present-day heritage sites are not evidence that the empire’s political authority survives.
